fr:title.text: forester-apple-sync blocks the Emacs daemon event loop

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: forester-apple-sync blocks the Emacs daemon event loop

fr:mainmatter.html:p: sync.sh invokes forester-apple-sync via emacsclient --eval '(forester-apple-sync)'. Because emacsclient --eval runs the function synchronously in the Emacs daemon's event loop, and forester-apple-sync makes one blocking osascript call per TODO, the entire Emacs process is unresponsive for the full duration of the sync (up to several seconds). The sync fires every 30 minutes via launchd, so this happens silently in the background and is easy to miss until it coincides with active editing.

There is no reason the daemon needs to be involved here at all — sync.sh already has a emacs --batch fallback path for when the daemon is unavailable. The batch path should be preferred for non-interactive bulk work, not just used as a fallback.

html:ul.html:li: Prefer batch over daemon for sync. Invert the sync.sh logic: always use emacs --batch -l ~/ocaml-forester/forester-org.el --eval '(forester-apple-sync)' for the launchd-triggered sync. The daemon path (emacsclient) can remain for manual SPC r s invocations where interactive feedback is wanted.

Run async inside the daemon. If the daemon path is kept, wrap the bulk sync body in make-process or async-start so osascript calls do not block the event loop. This is more complex but also fixes the SPC r s interactive path.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: See Automate Apple Reminders and Calendar sync for Forester TODOs for the broader sync architecture.

Resolution (2026-04-18). Took option 1. sync.sh's apple_sync is now batch-only (emacs --batch -l ~/ocaml-forester/forester-org.el --eval '(forester-apple-sync)') and the background invocation is re-enabled. The daemon branch is gone entirely — SPC r s also benefits, since forester-sync-all shells out to sync.sh via start-process, so neither the launchd path nor the interactive path touches the daemon event loop anymore. Batch also picks up latest forester-org.el from disk, which removes the previous "daemon was started before the elisp was updated" staleness case.

My editing environment for .tree files is a two-layer stack: the upstream forester.el major mode plus my own large forester-org.el extension. Both live in one repo at ~/forester.el, which is my fork of ToposInstitute/forester.el (origin = stschaef/forester.el, with upstream pointing at Topos).

forester.el (upstream, Topos Institute) — the base major mode: syntax/font-lock for forester markup, rainbow-delimiters, and a handful of wrapper commands. This is the file autoloaded for .tree buffers. I carry a few personal patches on top of upstream (hard-coded forest root, rg-based grep, forester-find-title).

forester-org.el (mine, ~168 KB, ~190 interactive commands) — an org-mode-style workflow layer built entirely on tags in .tree files, with no compiler modifications. It provides tree navigation/creation (find, capture, daily notes), TODO state management, an agenda buffer, a cached query engine (forester query all plus filter combinators) with result buffers, Apple Reminders/Calendar sync via osascript, eglot LSP integration, in-Emacs HTML preview via shr, and the SPC r keybinding suite via general.el. It was originally developed inside ~/ocaml-forester, then imported into the forester.el repo (commit c0f244c); it no longer lives in ocaml-forester.

How it loads. ~/.emacs.d/packages.el adds ~/forester.el to load-path, autoloads forester-mode for .tree files, and registers autoload stubs for the forester-org commands so keybinds.el can bind them by symbol (the commandp check passes before bodies exist). ~/.emacs.d/init.el then does (require 'forester-org) eagerly, after all config files run, to fill in the real command bodies before any keybinding fires.
Keybindings. The SPC r ... prefix and the Evil keymaps for forester-org-agenda-mode, forester-query-mode, and forester-preview-mode are defined in ~/.emacs.d/keybinds.el.
Not in use. ~/forester_emacs_mode (GitHub stschaef/forester-emacs-mode) is an early-2025 standalone forester.el that has been superseded by the ~/forester.el fork. It can be ignored.
Related: forester-apple-sync blocks the Emacs daemon event loop, Automate Apple Reminders and Calendar sync.

fr:title.text: Automate Apple Reminders and Calendar sync for Forester TODOs

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Automate Apple Reminders and Calendar sync for Forester TODOs

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Get Forester TODOs syncing into Apple Reminders (and scheduled work blocks into Apple Calendar) without per-tree manual pushes. The plumbing is already in place; what's missing is a bulk / automatic layer.

html:ul.html:li: forester-apple-push in forester-org.el pushes the current buffer to Apple Reminders (if tagged todo) or Apple Calendar (if tagged event).

forester-apple-pull pulls status changes back from Apple Reminders into the corresponding .tree files (matched by an apple-id meta entry — see the parser bug subtree below for why we don't write the literal markup here).
The AppleScript layer (forester-org--osascript) is reliable; osascript round-trips work.
Reminders list defaults to Forester (forester-org-reminders-list); calendar defaults to Forester (forester-org-calendar-name).
The schedule-day skill uses AppleScript directly to create time-blocked events on the Tasks calendar with start/end alarms and a forester:sss-XXXX marker in the notes. This works today.
Bidirectional grocery-list sync is fully working (see Manage Grocery lists) and is a good reference implementation for what a full todo sync should look like.
No bulk push. Current active TODO trees (~19 pending) are not in the Forester Reminders list — it has 4 total, 0 pending, so it has gone stale.
No automatic sync on save. Editing a TODO's status or due date does not propagate to the associated reminder.
No scheduled sync. No cron / launchd job runs forester-apple-pull or a bulk push periodically.

Milestone trees (new pattern — see this milestone) are not a TODO and should be excluded from any bulk sync. The sync should filter by \taxon{TODO} (or equivalently \tag{todo}) and skip anything with \taxon{Milestone}.
(A) Bulk push command — forester-sync-all-todos: iterate every .tree with or , call forester-org--push-reminder on each. Pair with a pull. Run manually at start of day.
(B) Save hook — after-save on any .tree under ~/forest/trees/: if it has \taxon{TODO} (and not \taxon{Milestone}), auto-push. Low latency, no cron needed.
(C) Launchd / cron — schedule (A) every N hours. Best for keeping Reminders fresh even when Emacs isn't open; worst for latency.
(A) + (B) together is probably the right answer: (A) for bootstrap and recovery, (B) for steady state.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The first bulk push from forester-apple-sync crashed on this very tree. The cause: forester-org--parse-meta is a regex that scans the entire file rather than only the frontmatter. The body originally contained an example showing how the apple-id meta is written, embedded in a ... block. The parser treated that example as a real frontmatter declaration, extracted its placeholder value as the apple-id, and fed it to AppleScript, which failed with Invalid index (-1719). The literal example is omitted from this tree on purpose to avoid re-triggering the bug.

Workaround applied. The prose on line 23 was rewritten to describe the meta entry by name rather than embedding the literal markup. This is a hack — any future tree that documents this meta key by writing the literal markup would re-trigger the bug.

Proper fix (not done). forester-org--parse-meta (and likely forester-org--parse-tag and forester-org--parse-taxon) should restrict their search to the frontmatter region — i.e. lines before the first body element such as a paragraph or subtree. That would also fix any other tree that mentions meta or tag declarations in its body.

Defensive secondary fix (also not done). forester-org--push-reminder could catch the Invalid index osascript error on the update path and fall back to creating a fresh reminder. Useful regardless of the parser fix, since stale apple-ids can also arise from the user manually deleting reminders.
